nodes.label: UX Smoothening Plan (PR1 + PR2)
nodes.rationale: Two sequential PRs: PR1 rewrites launcher copy, restructures composition, adds a tomorrow-countdown and softens the daily game-over screen; PR2 changes the first-load posture so the map is the homepage. UI vocabulary moves from 'free' to 'unlimited' while analytics event names stay unchanged for backwards compatibility.

nodes.label: useNextDailyCountdown hook
nodes.rationale: Computes hours/minutes until local midnight and ticks every 60s; the unit logic lives in the hook so the LauncherCountdown component test can stay small and clock-mocking is confined to one place.

nodes.label: LauncherCountdown component
nodes.rationale: Purely presentational 'Next puzzle in 4h 23m' line, mounted only when both modes are already played — it exists to give the exhausted-for-today state a forward-looking answer instead of a dead end.

nodes.label: Map-first load posture
nodes.rationale: useLauncherVisibility changes a single boolean rule so a bare hash returns visible:false — the map becomes the homepage and no modal blocks a cold visitor. Carries funnel risk, which is why the plan tracks it explicitly and pairs the change with a stateful header CTA so the daily stays reachable.

nodes.label: Stateful header CTA pill
nodes.rationale: Replaces the bare icon play button with a three-state pill plus a streak chip and a mobile combined form, wired to a new header_cta_clicked analytics event — it is the compensating affordance for removing the auto-opening launcher modal.

nodes.label: ensureLauncherDismissed / openLauncher e2e helpers
nodes.rationale: Renaming dismissLauncher to ensureLauncherDismissed encodes the new posture in the helper name: the launcher may or may not be open on a bare load, so the helper must be a conditional no-op rather than an unconditional dismissal. openLauncher is its inverse for tests that need the launcher visible.

nodes.label: 'free' to 'unlimited' vocabulary rename
nodes.rationale: UI vocabulary changes from 'free' (which reads as a pricing tier) to 'unlimited' (which reads as a play mode), but analytics event names deliberately stay on the old spelling so historical funnel data remains comparable.
